evidence: Shared state: task/tests/test.sh:104-113 starts ONE app on one DB_PATH; run_suite (203-210) runs gates (213) then scored (224) with 'rewardkit --max-concurrent-agent 1', so render/constraints then functional/polish/visual run sequentially against the same database; the order inside a suite is not fixed by the task, so every order must be tolerated. Mutations by each dimension: render prompt.md:9 'Do not create, move or send anything, and do not open any conversation'; constraints prompt.md:9 creates one job+candidate and 'Do not move, reject or message anything here'; polish/visual/functional gates each create their own suffixed job+card; polish prompt.md:14 'Use your own new job and cards ... never rely on another review's records', :16 'Never use Lena Fischer's conversation', and sends/drafts in Noor's (or another) conversation; visual prompt.md:14 is read-only after its gate ('Do not move cards or send messages'); functional mutates heavily (own J1/J2/J3, Tomas link, messages in Noor's/Tomas's conversations, restart). Pristine-seed assumptions and their protection: (1) functional Z (prompt.md:25) and hro_unread_counts read Lena Fischer's Product Designer unread = 1. Seed: reads USR-CAN3/APP-301 read_count 2 and APP-301 has 3 messages, the third from USR-REC3, so 1 is correct; no other dimension may touch that conversation (render no conversations, constraints no messages, polish explicit ban, visual no sends, candidate view only as Noor), and Z runs first inside functional with 'do not sign in as Lena again before K'. (2) Z/hro_restart read the seeded Platform Engineer order (Applied Greta, Ade, Marco; Screen Priya, Samuel — matches seed positions APP-105/106/108, APP-103/104) and Noor's note; every other dimension is confined to its own new jobs/cards or is read-only, and functional itself says 'Move nothing on that job'. State-relative wording elsewhere: app_context.md:29-31 'Other reviews may have added jobs, cards and messages; never rely on a starting count'; functional prompt.md:15 'Earlier reviews may have added jobs, cards and messages. Use your own new jobs and cards ... never rely on starting counts'; T fallback 'counts read relative to their values before you act'; T 'if that address is already on J2, open a new job J3'; Noor's 120-message conversation rows (hro_thread_latest 'most recent 30', hro_thread_earlier 'until none remain', hro_unread_scrolled_up 'one new message', U 'before and after') are all relative to what is observed, so polish/visual messages or reads on Noor's conversation do not break them; Mei's count is 'computed from the observed sequence'. Polish prompt.md:14 'If a message or note box already holds text from an earlier review, record it and clear it before typing your own' tolerates functional's leftover drafts; polish live-board/live-thread/failed-send/session-resume are all relative ('sent once', own cards). Visual grades presentation of whatever data exists ('a seeded job is fine', read-only). Adversarial attempts: (a) a conforming app failing because polish ran first and changed Noor's message count -> refuted, all Noor rows are relative; (b) a conforming app failing because a gate/polish review moved seeded Platform Engineer cards or messaged Lena -> refuted, those prompts forbid it; (c) a broken app passing because a later dimension expects seed values an earlier dimension destroyed -> none found. Residual latent P3 (not a defect): functional lacks polish's 'clear leftover box text' sentence; if polish ran first and its session-resume left Rafael's server-stored draft in the conversation that functional T later uses (only plausible under the Data Analyst fallback or when Noor's conversation is chosen as the 'another conversation'), typed text would append to it; a conforming app still keeps the draft with its conversation and the sent message still keeps its line break, so no misgrade is expected. Runtime: raw-evidence-index scope says 'Full configured grading/workload ... are absent'; no configured multi-dimension judge run exercised the cross-dimension ordering, so this verdict rests on prompt/seed inspection (the row's verification procedure is wording-based).
